newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila eyes tax amnesty for firms going public.
newsitem.headline: Manila eyes tax amnesty for firms going public.

text.p: The Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) has asked the Department of Finance to look into the possibility of granting tax amnesty to companies going public, PSE board member Ramon Garcia said on Thursday.
Garcia told reporters that the amnesty, which would be limited to one year, should encourage family-held corporations to offer their shares to the public.
A number of family-held corporations have been under investigation for tax evasion.

"Why not grant a one-year tax amnesty to any company that's going to be listed? What kind of revenues will the government lose anyway if the companies are not reporting their taxes. But once they list, you can be sure that they will be paying their taxes," Garcia said.
The Department of Finance is understood to be studying the proposal, he said.
The tax amnesty has been offered in other Asian countries to spur the growth of the capital market, Garcia added.
